title: MORI traffic overview: IO and EP
description: IO and EP traffic together, on the same links and the same time axis: what each puts on XGMI and on RDMA over time (do they take turns or overlap, how close to what the links carry). Details per GPU, per NIC and GPU to GPU are in the IO and the EP dashboard.

list.name: host
list.label: Host
list.description: The GPUs of these hosts: every host that ran EP or sent IO within the time range.

list.name: gpu
list.label: GPU
list.description: All, or the GPUs to look at: the charts then shows what these GPUs send (cpu = host memory, IO only).

list.name: res
list.label: Rate window
list.description: The time every rate on this page is averaged over. auto: what the data source suggests (20 s for scraped data). 1ms to 500ms are for the millisecond data source: the counters advance one batch at a time (an IO transfer when it is submitted or completes, an EP launch when it ends), so a window of a millisecond or two shows a train of spikes and a longer one the average over several batches. With scraped data (a sample every 5 s) a window under about 10 s finds no two samples and the charts are empty.

list.name: window
list.label: Average over
list.description: Window of the tiles and of the GPU to GPU matrices. The charts over time follow the dashboard's own resolution. 5s and 10s are for the millisecond data source: scraped data has a point every few seconds.

list.name: rpair
list.label: Hosts with RDMA between them

list.name: xgmi_limit
list.label: XGMI limit per GPU (GB/s)
list.description: The dashed line in the XGMI chart: what one GPU can send over XGMI to all its peers together, times the GPUs shown. 291.25 is the payload measured on 8 x MI300X with every GPU sending to the 7 others (2.33 TB/s for the node; the line rate, 7 links x 64 GB/s, is not reachable). Set it for other hardware.

panels.title: Metrics sampling: 1/N = one call in N is counted (EP: a dispatch with its combine; IO: a put / get), in every running process

panels.description: The sampling rate of the metrics, set for every MORI process Prometheus scrapes at this moment, while they run. 1/1: every EP dispatch (with its combine) and every IO transfer is counted. 1/8, 1/64, 1/100: one in so many is counted and counts so many times, so the charts keep showing the same quantities, a little noisier, and the counting costs less. off: nothing is counted and the charts of that side go to zero. The ring marks the rate in effect now (red: off), whatever time range the page shows; it moves at the next refresh after a click. Processes started later begin with their own setting (MORI_METRICS_SAMPLE_EP / _IO, default 1/1). Needs the sampling gateway of up.sh.

panels.description: How often Prometheus reads (scrapes) /metrics of every MORI process: one point per process and series that often, for the data source mori-traffic. A click rewrites scrape_interval in Prometheus' configuration and reloads it. Shorter: finer charts and shorter rate windows possible (a rate needs two samples in its window), more load on Prometheus and the processes. Does not change the millisecond data source (mori-traffic-ms), which the processes push to themselves. The ring marks the interval in effect. Needs the sampling gateway of traffic.sh.

panels.title: IO and EP on the same links, over time (bytes / wall time)
XGMI: sent by IO and by EP
panels.description: Bytes per second the selected GPUs send over XGMI, all of them together: for the IO engines, and as EP payload (dispatch and combine). The thin grey line is the two added up: what XGMI carries in total. Dashed: what it can carry, the XGMI limit per GPU (variable at the top; 291.25 GB/s measured on MI300X, 2.33 TB/s for 8 GPUs) times the selected GPUs that send. Read the two lines against each other: peaks that alternate mean IO and EP take turns on these links; peaks at the same time mean both are on them at once.

targets.expr: count(count by (h, g) (label_replace(label_replace(last_over_time(mori_io_submitted_bytes_total{src_host=~"$host",src_gpu=~"$gpu",src_gpu!="cpu",backend="xgmi"}[$__range] @ end()), "h", "$1", "src_host", "(.*)"), "g", "$1", "src_gpu", "(.*)") or label_replace(label_replace(last_over_time(mori_ep_xgmi_bytes_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",direction="tx"}[$__range] @ end()), "h", "$1", "host", "(.*)"), "g", "$1", "gpu", "(.*)"))) * $xgmi_limit * 1e9

panels.title: RDMA: sent by IO and by EP
panels.description: Bytes per second the selected GPUs send over RDMA through their NICs, all of them together: for the IO engines, and what the GPUs put on RDMA themselves (EP between nodes). The thin grey line is the two added up. Read the two lines against each other: peaks that alternate mean IO and EP take turns on these links; peaks at the same time mean both are on them at once.

panels.title: RDMA per GPU: IO

panels.title: EP kernels: how much data a dispatch / combine moves, and how long it takes
EP bytes per call
panels.description: How much data one dispatch and one combine of a rank moves: the bytes of the tokens a dispatch delivers to the rank's experts, and of the tokens a combine gives back, tokens that stay on the GPU included (what an EP benchmark reports as bytes), divided by the calls; averaged over the selected GPUs. Divided by the kernel time per call on the right it is the kernel bandwidth (EP dashboard).

targets.expr: sum by (op) ((sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) ((rate(mori_ep_tokens_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="dispatch",direction="rx",path!="rdma"}[$res]) or rate(mori_ep_tokens_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="combine",direction="tx",path!="rdma"}[$res]))) * sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) ((rate(mori_ep_xgmi_bytes_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="dispatch",direction="rx"}[$res]) or rate(mori_ep_xgmi_bytes_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="combine",direction="tx"}[$res]))) / (sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) ((rate(mori_ep_tokens_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="dispatch",direction="rx",path="xgmi"}[$res]) or rate(mori_ep_tokens_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="combine",direction="tx",path="xgmi"}[$res]))) > 0)) and on (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) (rate(mori_ep_calls_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu"}[$res]))) / sum by (op) (sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) (rate(mori_ep_calls_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu"}[$res])) and on (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) (sum by (host, gpu, rank, impl, op) ((rate(mori_ep_tokens_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="dispatch",direction="rx",path="xgmi"}[$res]) or rate(mori_ep_tokens_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu",op="combine",direction="tx",path="xgmi"}[$res]))) > 0))

panels.title: EP kernel time per call
panels.description: Time one dispatch and one combine take, measured on the device from the start of the kernel to its end (an inter-node dispatch or combine: its whole sequence of launches): kernel seconds / calls, averaged over the selected GPUs.

targets.expr: sum by (op) (rate(mori_ep_kernel_seconds_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu"}[$res])) / (sum by (op) (rate(mori_ep_calls_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu"}[$res]) and on (host, gpu, rank, impl, op, kernel) rate(mori_ep_kernel_seconds_total{host=~"$host",gpu=~"$gpu"}[$res])) > 0)

panels.title: IO transfers: how much a put / get carries, and how long it takes
IO bytes per transfer
panels.description: How much data one put (write) and one get (read) carries: bytes submitted / transfers submitted, for the transfers the selected GPUs issue, by backend. Dashed: get.

panels.title: IO time per transfer
panels.description: How long one put (write) and one get (read) takes, from its submission to its completion: the time the transfers took / the transfers that completed, for the transfers the selected GPUs issue, by backend. Dashed: get. RDMA: until the completion was processed. XGMI: until the caller looked at the transfer's status, so this is the time the caller saw.
